catalog_quote: Идеальным примером, где место ударения зависит от фонетического фактора, является коми-язьвинский диалект. В неодносложных словах этого диалекта ударение не падает на гласные исконно верхнего подъема 1-го слога (i < *i, u < *u, ө < *i̮) — в этом случае акцент находится на каком-нибудь гласном непервого слога. Если же в первом слоге стоят гласные исконно среднего или нижнего подъема (e, o, ȯ, a, u < *o̭, ɯ < *ȯ̭), то ударение падает на них. Таким образом ударение падает на более звучные гласные, т. е. место ударения в слове зависит от качества (сонорности) гласных, наличествующих в этом слове. Таким образом ударение падает на более звучные гласные, т. е. место ударения в слове зависит от качества (сонорности) гласных ... new_statements.translation: The ideal example of stress placement depending on a phonetic factor is the Komi-Yazva dialect. In polysyllabic words of this dialect stress does not fall on first-syllable vowels that are etymologically high (i < *i, u < *u, ө < *i̮) — in that case the accent is on some vowel of a non-first syllable. If, however, the first syllable contains vowels that are etymologically mid or low (e, o, ȯ, a, u < *o̭, ü < *ȯ̭), the stress falls on them. Thus stress falls on the more sonorous vowels, i.e. the place of stress in the word depends on the quality (sonority) of the vowels present in the word ... On a weakly sonorous first-syllable vowel stress never falls at all: muni·s 'he left', munө· 'goes', etc.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Quality (sonority)-sensitive, unbounded: primary stress goes to the leftmost 'heavy' vowel, where heavy = non-high vowels a, o, ȯ, e plus those surface high u, ü, i that continue Proto-Komi closed mid *o̭, *ȯ̭, *ḙ (i.e. correspond to o, e̮/ö, e in other Komi dialects); light = u, i from *u, *i and ө (< *i̮, phonetically mid today but patterning as high). In practice stress is on the first syllable whenever its vowel is heavy; a light first-syllable vowel is never stressed and stress moves right to a later (heavy) syllable; if the word has only light vowels it is end-stressed (default-to-final stated explicitly by Itkonen 1955: 29 'Gibt es nur leichte Vokale im Worte, so ist das Wort endbetont', cf. Lytkin's munө· 'идет', Itkonen's buzginө·; Lytkin 1961: 33-34 via Normanskaja 2018: 175 adds that first-syllable ө always passes stress to the following syllable). Lytkin stresses there is no initial-stress tendency at all. Monosyllables trivially stressed.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described by Lytkin 1970 or Itkonen 1955 for Komi-Yazva (StressTyp2 codes secondary stress absent).
new_statements.exceptions: Lytkin 1970: 254-255 'единичные случаи морфологизации': (a) stress on the syllable preceding comparative -žik regardless of its vowel (pö·riś 'old' ~ pö·riśžik); (b) some suffixes attract stress against the quality principle: ordinal -öt (kvi·miś ~ kvimö·t 'third'), diminutive -ik, emphatic -ik/-i; (c) when stress leaves a light-vowel root, preference order among suffixes: plural > case > possessive; (d) certain derivational suffixes (-ölt, causative -öt, adjectival -öl, verbal -ör) keep the stress once it reaches them rather than passing it on to later heavy vowels — but only when syll 1 has a light vowel, so this is 'partial morphologisation within the quality-vocalic system'. Normanskaja 2018: 175 (after Lytkin 1961) hedges 'в большинстве случаев'; Itkonen 'gewöhnlich'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress in citation/inflected word forms ('в неодносложных словах', 'место ударения в слове'); examples include case-inflected forms (mu ~ muśa·ń, va ~ vaśa·ń) so the domain is the phonological word including suffixes. Weight criterion is vowel quality (height/sonority), partly etymological/lexical for surface u, ü, i; no role for vowel length or codas.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the Komi-Yazva (Jaz'va, коми-язьвинский, Itkonen's 'Ostpermjakisch') variety of the upper Yazva river, Krasnovishersk district, Perm krai = Glottolog komi1277. Lytkin 1970 and Osnovy 1976 call it 'коми-язьвинский диалект / наречие'. NOTE: the existing catalog unit keyed komi1268 (Komi-Zyrian;, source Itkonen 1955) in fact codes this same lect (its own record says 'komi1277 (lect described)'); the StressTyp2 entry for this language 'Yazva', WALS yzv and legacy ST the StressTyp2 entry for this language 'Komi' are all this variety. Komi-Zyrian proper (komi1268) has a weight-blind initial tendency and Komi-Permyak proper (komi1269) stem-based ('осново-разноместное') stress, per the same sources. The closely similar quality-driven system of the On'kovo subdialect of Komi-Permyak (Lytkin 1970: 250, 257; Osnovy 1976 §19) is a different lect (komi1269).

sources.note: p. 250 (page image verified): Komi-Yazva is the 'ideal example' of phonetically conditioned stress: in polysyllables stress does not fall on etymologically high 1st-syllable vowels (i<*i, u<*u, ө<*i̮) and then lies on some non-first syllable; if the 1st syllable has an etymologically mid/low vowel (e, o, ȯ, a, u<*o̭, ü<*ȯ̭) it is stressed; 'качественно-вокальное ударение'; no tendency to initial stress (muni·s, munө·). p. 251: the fixing of stress on sonorous vowels predates the merger of closed *o̭ *ḙ *ȯ̭ with u i ü, so u,i,ü from those are always stressed in syll 1, u,i,ü from *u *i *ü uns…

sources.note: pp. 28-29 (txt ll. 389-431 re-read): in 'Ostpermjakisch' (= Komi-Yazva) the accent is mobile and depends on vowel aperture; reflexes of Proto-Permic u, i̮, i are «leicht», all others «schwer»; 'Der Akzent ist gewöhnlich in der Silbe zu finden, die den ersten «schweren» Vokal hat. Gibt es nur «leichte» Vokale im Worte, so ist das Wort endbetont' (po·tkөtnө, go·rtiśań ~ juka·śnө ~ buzginө·, pөčkiśa·ń); mostly initial, shifting only when syll 1 has a high vowel. Supplies the explicit default-to-final clause; this is the source StressTyp2/WALS cite.
